newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries little changed at opening on Friday.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries little changed at opening on Friday.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities were narrowly range bound at Friday's opening with dealers expecting little movement or volume.

The only data due were the Treasury Department's monthly budget data for May in which economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, a $49.4 billion deficit versus a surplus of $93.9 billion in September. Those numbers were due at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia also was set to release its semiannual Livingston survey at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, a poll of private forecasters on the economy.
On Thursday the Philadelphia Fed reported that its business activity index rose to 25.2 in June from 1.6 in May, but the bond market was able to shake the number off after an initial downtrade.

"If you can, leave early. Otherwise find something interesting to do like the crossword puzzle, but try not to finish the newspaper before 9 a.m.," said the chief trader at a primary dealership, speaking of how much he expected the market to move this session.
He said the market enjoyed a solid week and was holding firm with little to threaten current bullish sentiment.

The trader said there would be some supply next week, but that would likely be easily absorbed. The Treasury will auction $15.5 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday and $11.5 of five-year notes on Wednesday.
He said with options expiring this session the September T-bond contract was likely to remain in 112 range.
"By this afternoon half (of traders) were likely to be golfing or watching it," he said.
The release of budget data could affect the market a little, but that was unlikely, he said.
